before: A Java declaration that groups members such as fields and methods.
after: A declaration that groups data fields and methods for Java objects.

before: A named operation declared in a Java class or interface; it may accept parameters and return a result.
after: A named operation inside a class or interface. It can receive inputs and may return an answer.

before: A standard library class that reads and can convert input tokens.
after: A Java reader that splits input into tokens and can read values such as integers.

before: A signed 32-bit whole-number primitive type.
after: A whole-number type that stores values from -2147483648 through 2147483647.

before: A primitive type with exactly the values true and false.
after: A type with two possible values: true and false.

before: Instructions in Java class files that the JVM executes.
after: Instructions stored in compiled class files for the Java Virtual Machine to run.

before: A built-in Java numeric type with specified representation and operations.
after: A built-in number type, such as int or double, with its own range and calculation rules.

before: An arithmetic operation that reports overflow instead of silently returning a wrapped result.
after: A calculation that reports when its result is too large or too small for the number type.

before: Whether two references point to the same object, rather than merely equal content.
after: Whether two references point to one object. Separate objects may still hold equal data.

before: One 16-bit unit used in Java char and String storage.
after: One numbered text-storage unit. A Java char holds one unit; some Unicode code points need two.

before: A mutable Java object for assembling a character sequence.
after: A Java object for building text that can change.

before: A reference value that does not refer to any object.
after: A reference value that points to no object.

before: An expression that selects and returns a result from matching cases.
after: A switch that chooses a matching case and produces a result value.

before: A Java loop that visits values supplied by an array or iterable.
after: A loop that visits the items supplied by an array or another iterable collection.

before: A Java list implementation that can change its number of elements.
after: An ordered Java list that can gain or lose items.

before: Retrieving a mapped value using its key rather than a sequence position.
after: Finding a stored value by its key instead of by a numbered position.

before: Whether a value belongs to a collection of distinct members.
after: Whether a value is present in a set, which keeps each distinct member once.

before: A final method parameter that collects a variable number of supplied values into an array.
after: The last input parameter, marked with ..., which gathers a changing number of supplied values into an array.

before: Giving a method a copy of the supplied primitive value or reference value.
after: Giving a method a copy of each input value. A copied object reference can still point to the same object.

before: Control access to representation through operations that maintain a class’s rules.
after: Keep data and its allowed operations together, using controlled access to protect the object's rules.

before: A variable assigned only as permitted during initialization; a final reference does not freeze its object.
after: A variable that can be assigned only once. If it points to an object, that object's contents may still change.

before: A subclass supplies an implementation of an inherited instance method with a compatible signature.
after: A child class supplies its own version of an inherited instance method with matching inputs and a compatible result type.

before: A class that cannot be instantiated directly and may require subclasses to implement abstract methods.
after: A class that cannot be created directly. Concrete child classes provide any required method bodies.

before: A data-carrier class whose declared components determine generated accessors and value-oriented methods.
after: A compact Java class for named data components, with generated construction, reading, comparison, hashing, and display methods.

before: A type hierarchy whose permitted direct subtypes are explicitly controlled.
after: A set of related types where a parent limits which direct child types are allowed.

before: A type with a fixed declared set of named instances.
after: A Java type with a fixed set of named values.

before: Logically equal objects must have equal hash codes; a collision does not imply equality.
after: Objects that compare equal must have the same hash code. Different objects can also share a hash code.

before: A placeholder type used to define a family of type-checked classes or methods.
after: A placeholder for a type chosen when a class or method is used.

before: A type restriction that makes specified operations available inside generic code.
after: A rule limiting a generic type choice so the code can rely on certain operations being available.

before: An unknown type with an upper or lower bound that controls safe generic reads and writes.
after: An unknown generic type limited with extends or super, which controls what can safely be read or added.

before: Convert a wrapper reference to its primitive value; null cannot be unboxed.
after: Get a primitive value, such as int, from its wrapper object. Unboxing null fails.

before: An exception type subject to Java’s compile-time catch-or-declare requirement.
after: An exception Java requires you to catch or declare with throws.

before: A statement that automatically closes declared resources when its block exits.
after: A try block that automatically calls close on its managed resources when the block exits.

before: A container representing either one non-null value or no value.
after: An object holding either a present non-null value or no value.

before: A runtime type test that binds a variable of the tested type on a successful match.
after: A check that an object has a stated type, giving it a usable local name when the check succeeds.

before: Build behavior by holding and using collaborator objects rather than inheriting all behavior.
after: Build an object's behavior by having it use other objects as helpers.

before: A local binding that is not reassigned and can therefore be captured by a lambda.
after: A local variable that is not reassigned after its starting value, even without the final keyword.

before: Syntax adapting an existing compatible method to a functional interface.
after: A way to supply an existing method as an operation to call later.

before: A source followed by intermediate operations and a terminal operation.
after: A source of values followed by processing steps and an operation that finishes the query.

before: A collector used inside another collector to process each subgroup.
after: A gathering rule used inside another gathering rule, such as counting the items in each group.

before: A stream pipeline that cannot be consumed again after a terminal operation.
after: A stream that must not be used again after an operation finishes its query.

before: Writing at the end of existing file contents rather than replacing them.
after: Write at the end of a file while keeping its earlier contents.

before: A defined mapping between text and byte sequences.
after: Rules for turning text into bytes and reading those bytes back as text.

before: Checking parsed settings against the constraints required by the program.
after: Check that settings can be read and that their values obey the program's rules.

before: A point on the time line, independent of its local calendar representation.
after: One moment on the timeline, regardless of the local date or time used to show it.

before: For a positive scale, the number of digits to the right of the decimal point.
after: For a positive scale, the number of digits kept after the decimal point.

before: Combining an ordering key with further tie-break ordering rules.
after: Use one ordering rule first, then another rule when the first one gives a tie.

before: An independent structural copy that prevents callers from changing the stored collection through the returned list.
after: A snapshot that keeps a collection's current items when its source later changes. The item objects may still be shared.

before: Roots or archives searched for classes outside named-module resolution.
after: Folders or archives Java searches for classes outside named modules, starting from the listed roots.

before: A collection of packages governed by an explicit module descriptor.
after: A group of packages with a name and rules declared in module-info.java.

before: A required source or artifact intentionally supplied to the build rather than accidentally available.
after: Needed code deliberately supplied to a build, with its source or library details recorded.

before: The policy controlling how long annotation metadata is retained and whether runtime reflection can observe it.
after: A rule for how long annotation information is kept and whether running code can inspect it.

before: A condition that throws on failure independently of the optional Java assertion switch.
after: An ordinary condition that reports a failed test by throwing, without needing the assert launch flag.

before: Information that helps locate a failed assumption rather than merely hiding a failure.
after: Information that helps find why an operation failed, such as an error type and the call where it arose.

before: A Java memory-model ordering relationship that establishes visibility of earlier actions to later ones.
after: A Java ordering guarantee that makes earlier actions visible to later actions. A successful join provides such a guarantee.

before: The lock associated with an object and used by synchronized code to coordinate access.
after: An object's built-in lock, used by synchronized code to coordinate access.

before: An update that takes effect as one indivisible operation with respect to concurrent access.
after: A change that acts as one indivisible step when several threads use the value.

before: A lightweight Java thread scheduled by the runtime rather than a dedicated platform thread per task.
after: A lightweight thread scheduled by Java, useful for many tasks that spend time waiting.

before: A computation dependent on another asynchronous result, not necessarily running on a new thread.
after: Work connected to another result's completion. It does not necessarily run on a new thread.

before: Responsibility for releasing an external resource at a defined lifetime boundary.
after: Responsibility for closing an external resource at the right point in its use.

before: A condition that every valid model instance and transition must preserve.
after: A rule that must remain true whenever the model is created or updated.
